searchText: Question on this part of the LC spec: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/altair/light-client/full-node.md#create_light_client_bootstrap Given that `hash_tree_root(state) != state.latest_block_header.state_root`, what exactly is `state.latest_block_header.state_root` referring to or used for? Edit: is it the state root we expect from applying the latest block to `state`? <etan_status> it is hash_tree_root() of the BeaconState after applying the corresponding BeaconBlock <etan_status> it is not the EL block header state_root, but instead the CL BeaconState root the state root is set in `process_slot` where the state root of the state after applying the previous block (which the `latest_block_header` corresponds to) is written to that location, see code here: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/phase0/beacon-chain.md#beacon-chain-state-transition-function there is a circular dependency so the state root has to be written after updating the state <@539495253418180618> I think I see.. but in this case, does this indicate that the most recent `BeaconState` always has `state.latest_block.header.state_root == Bytes32()` ? as you would only update `latest_block_header.state_root` on application of the _next_ block it is "cleared" for each block -- see here: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/phase0/beacon-chain.md#block-header -- and then at the start of the next slot (regardless of block!) you insert the correct state root this is done so that the state/block roots that are written to the history accumulator are correct (see the rest of `process_slot`) I see.. another way to say it is, for the `state` at slot `n` the `state.latest_block_header` corresponds to the block with slot `n-1`, and `state.latest_block_header.state_root` is correctly set to `hash_tree_root(state)` only after receiving some block with slot `x > n`? the `latest_block_header` is for the block at slot `n` (or the last block, whenever that was) -- the only thing missing is the state root bc you can't compute the state root if you need the state root (the circular dep here) Ah okay right, and the state root will be set on the next call to `process_slot`, which should be when receiving a block with slot `> n`

excerpts.author: mynervini
excerpts.content:
Question on this part of the LC spec: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/altair/light-client/full-node.md#create_light_client_bootstrap
Given that `hash_tree_root(state) != state.latest_block_header.state_root`, what exactly is `state.latest_block_header.state_root` referring to or used for?
Edit: is it the state root we expect from applying the latest block to `state`?

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <etan_status> it is hash_tree_root() of the BeaconState after applying the corresponding BeaconBlock

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <etan_status> it is not the EL block header state_root, but instead the CL BeaconState root

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: the state root is set in `process_slot` where the state root of the state after applying the previous block (which the `latest_block_header` corresponds to) is written to that location, see code here: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/phase0/beacon-chain.md#beacon-chain-state-transition-function

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: there is a circular dependency so the state root has to be written after updating the state

excerpts.author: mynervini
excerpts.content: <@539495253418180618> I think I see.. but in this case, does this indicate that the most recent `BeaconState` always has `state.latest_block.header.state_root == Bytes32()` ? as you would only update `latest_block_header.state_root` on application of the _next_ block

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: it is "cleared" for each block -- see here: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/phase0/beacon-chain.md#block-header -- and then at the start of the next slot (regardless of block!) you insert the correct state root

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: this is done so that the state/block roots that are written to the history accumulator are correct

excerpts.author: mynervini
excerpts.content: I see.. another way to say it is, for the `state` at slot `n` the `state.latest_block_header`  corresponds to the block with slot `n-1`, and `state.latest_block_header.state_root` is correctly set to `hash_tree_root(state)` only after receiving some block with slot `x > n`?

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: the `latest_block_header` is for the block at slot `n` (or the last block, whenever that was) -- the only thing missing is the state root bc you can't compute the state root if you need the state root (the circular dep here)

excerpts.author: mynervini
excerpts.content: Ah okay right, and the state root will be set on the next call to `process_slot`, which should be when receiving a block with slot `> n`
